definition.simple: The top layer of the forest made of branches and leaves that acts like a big umbrella.
definition.academic: The uppermost continuous layer of a forest, formed by the crowns of the tallest trees, which intercepts sunlight and rainfall.

examples: Monkeys and birds often live in the forest canopy.
The canopy blocks most of the sunlight from reaching the ground.

common_misconceptions: People often think a forest only has trees on the ground, forgetting the different horizontal layers like the canopy above.
ai_context.tutor_hint: Ask the student what acts like an umbrella for the animals on the ground when it rains in a forest.
